claims.text: Premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on Zr-alloy substrates is caused by elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
A thin Al2O3 interlayer should be placed between the elemental Cr coating and the Zr-alloy substrate.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer must be dense and adherent.
The Al2O3 interlayer will act as a diffusion barrier to Cr and Zr.
The Al2O3 interlayer will prevent elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Suppressing Cr-Zr interdiffusion will preserve the integrity of the Cr coating.
The modified coating will maintain the protective properties of elemental Cr.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated Zr-alloy substrate, the Al2O3-interlayer system will have improved corrosion resistance.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the Al2O3-interlayer system will have improved oxidation resistance.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the Al2O3-interlayer system will exhibit less Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the Al2O3-interlayer system will have enhanced coating durability.
The hypothesis is intended to apply over 900-1300 degrees Celsius.
The hypothesis is intended to apply for exposure times up to 100 days.
The modified coating will remain protective in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The modified coating will remain protective during normal subcritical-water operation.
Radiation and mechanical stress may affect the performance of the proposed interlayer.

contradictions.description: The single stated temperature range of 900-1300 degrees Celsius is assigned to both high-temperature steam and subcritical water. Subcritical liquid-water operation cannot occur in that temperature range; separate normal-operation and accident temperature boundaries are needed.
